ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a horizontally placed parallel-plate capacitor, labeled C, with two plates facing each other above and below, and on the left a double-headed arrow marks the plate separation as d. Between the plates there is a horizontal dashed line, and the height from the dashed line to the lower plate is labeled d/3, indicating the initial liquid level height. In the circuit on the right, the capacitor is connected to a resistor R, so the time constant sought should be treated according to an RC circuit. Reasoning: The liquid is below and the air is above, and the two are layered along the direction of the electric field, so it is equivalent to two capacitors of the same area in series. Let the liquid height be h(t). Initially h(0)=d/3, and the liquid level descends at constant speed V, so h(t)=d/3 - Vt. The plate area A=1, and the dielectric constant of the liquid K=2. The series equivalent capacitance satisfies 1/C(t) = (d-h)/(ε0 A) + h/(K ε0 A). Substituting A=1, K=2, gives 1/C(t) = [d-h+h/2]/ε0 = [d-h/2]/ε0, so C(t)=ε0/[d-h(t)/2]. Substituting h(t)=d/3 - Vt: d-h(t)/2 = d - (d/3 - Vt)/2 = d - d/6 + Vt/2 = 5d/6 + Vt/2 = (5d+3Vt)/6. Therefore C(t)=6ε0/(5d+3Vt). The RC time constant is τ(t)=R C(t), so τ(t)=6ε0R/(5d+3Vt).

Model the air slab of thickness d-h and the liquid slab of thickness h as two capacitors in series with the same plate area. Use 1/C = (d-h)/(epsilon_0 A) + h/(K epsilon_0 A). Substitute A=1, K=2, and h(t), giving C(t)=epsilon_0/[d-h(t)+h(t)/2]=6epsilon_0/(5d+3Vt). Then use the RC time constant rule tau(t)=R C(t) to obtain tau(t)=6epsilon_0 R/(5d+3Vt).

claims.source: The series equivalent capacitance satisfies 1/C(t) = (d-h)/(ε0 A) + h/(K ε0 A)

claims.claim: Substituting A=1, K=2 gives 1/C(t) = [d-h+h/2]/ε0.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Substituting A=1, K=2, gives 1/C(t) = [d-h+h/2]/ε0

claims.claim: [d-h+h/2]/ε0 can be simplified to [d-h/2]/ε0.
claims.label: reasoning
reasoning
claims.source: Therefore C(t)=ε0/[d-h(t)/2]

claims.claim: After substituting h(t)=d/3 - Vt, d-h(t)/2 = (5d+3Vt)/6.

claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore C(t)=6ε0/(5d+3Vt)

claims.claim: The RC time constant is τ(t)=R C(t).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The RC time constant is τ(t)=R C(t)

claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore τ(t)=6ε0R/(5d+3Vt)
